issues.display_title: Issue #19: Resolve Incorrect CID Assignment on Google Tour Import by Utilizing PlaceID-to-CID Extraction
issues.main_description_html:
PlaceID to CID Validation & Auto-Sync Implementation

Technical documentation for the CID validation, in-memory extraction, and cache synchronization flow on the /places and /places/details endpoints in branch feat/validate-cid-convert.

1. Background & Problem Statement

Prior to this update, inconsistent and corrupted CID values were observed in the Typesense cache (places_cr collection):

  1. Incorrect CID / PlaceID Leakage:
    • The Google Place Details API frequently omits the ?cid= query parameter in modern Google Maps URLs (result.url).
    • The legacy code contained a flawed fallback: when cidParam was empty, resultCID defaulted to detailsResponse.Result.PlaceID (e.g., "ChIJN1t_t...").
    • Consequently, the string PlaceID was permanently stored in the cid column of Typesense.
  2. Lack of Cache Expiration (No TTL in Typesense):
    • Unlike Redis, which supports automatic key expiration (EXPIRE / TTL), Typesense collections persist documents indefinitely unless explicitly deleted or overwritten.
    • Once a place record with a corrupted or missing CID was saved to Typesense, all subsequent requests served this flawed cache entry.
  3. External Network Overhead:
    • Validating every record via external HTTP calls introduces network latency, HTTP timeouts, and potential outages if the external service becomes unavailable.

2. Updated Flow Architecture

The updated logic is implemented for place detail queries:

  • GET /places
  • GET /places/details

Flow Diagram:

Request: GET /places?place_id=... (or ?cid=...)
                      │
                      ▼
         Search in Typesense (places_cr)
                      │
        ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
        ▼                           ▼
[FOUND in Typesense]         [NOT FOUND in Typesense]
        │                           │
        ▼                           ▼
In-Memory CID Extraction      Search Google Places API
(ExtractCIDFromPlaceID)       (Original Google Fallback Flow)
        │                           │
   Does CID Mismatch or Empty?      ▼
        │                     Auto-save to Typesense
   ┌────┴────┐                (Background Goroutine)
   ▼         ▼                      │
[MISMATCH] [MATCH]                  │
   │         │                      │
Update CID   │                      │
in Typesense │                      │
(Background) │                      │
   │         │                      │
   └────┬────┘                      │
        │                           │
        ▼                           ▼
 Return Response to Client   Return Response to Client
 (models.PlaceDetails response schema remains identical)

Flow Rules:

  1. If FOUND in Typesense:
    • The CID is extracted and verified directly from place_id in-memory.
    • CID Mismatch or Empty: details.CID is updated with the valid extracted CID, updated_at is refreshed, and the record is upserted to Typesense asynchronously in the background.
    • CID Matches: The cached details are returned immediately (fast return) without unnecessary write operations.
  2. If NOT FOUND in Typesense:
    • Executes the original Google Places API fallback (getGooglePlaceDetails).
    • The Google response is auto-saved to Typesense in the background.
  3. Response Schema Contract:
    • Zero response changes. The returned JSON structure strictly preserves models.PlaceDetails. Existing encryption controls (ec) and authentication bypass options (auth) remain completely unchanged.

3. Technical Implementation Details

All changes are implemented in services/places.go and verified in services/places_test.go:

A. Native In-Memory CID Extraction (ExtractCIDFromPlaceID)

Google business Place IDs (starting with ChIJ, GhIJ, etc.) store the numeric CID in the final 8 bytes of the URL-safe Base64-decoded binary payload following the first 'J' character.
This function decodes and extracts the CID directly in Go:

  • Execution Time: ~0 ms (pure memory operations, zero network overhead).
  • Dependencies: Go standard library only (encoding/base64, encoding/binary, strconv, strings).
  • Output: 100% identical to the Python implementation in the placeid2cid service.
func ExtractCIDFromPlaceID(placeID string) (string, error) {
    idx := strings.Index(placeID, "J")
    if idx == -1 || idx < 3 {
        return "", fmt.Errorf("PlaceID format not recognised")
    }
    b64Part := placeID[idx+1:]
    if pad := len(b64Part) % 4; pad != 0 {
        b64Part += strings.Repeat("=", 4-pad)
    }
    data, err := base64.URLEncoding.DecodeString(b64Part)
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }
    if len(data) < 8 {
        return "", fmt.Errorf("Decoded payload too short for CID")
    }
    cid := binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(data[len(data)-8:])
    return strconv.FormatUint(cid, 10), nil
}

B. Validation & Asynchronous Cache Sync (validateAndSyncCID)

Verifies whether the cached CID in Typesense matches the decoded CID:

  • If different or empty, updates details.CID and triggers UpsertPlaceToTypesense inside a background goroutine.
  • Passes a struct copy (placeCopy models.PlaceDetails) into the goroutine to prevent data races during JSON serialization.

C. HTTP Fallback Support (ConvertPlaceIDToCID & FlexibleCID)

For scenarios where HTTP validation is explicitly required via PLACEID_CONVERT_URL, the service supports fallback to the REST endpoint. The custom FlexibleCID unmarshaler prevents precision loss when handling 64-bit unsigned integers from JSON responses.

4. Testing & Verification

Unit tests are provided in services/places_test.go:

go test -v ./services

Test Coverage:

  • TestExtractCIDFromPlaceID: Verifies offline decoding accuracy against Sydney Opera House (10281119596374313554) and other valid/invalid Place IDs.
  • TestFlexibleCID_UnmarshalJSON: Validates unmarshaling large unsigned 64-bit integers without precision loss.
  • TestConvertPlaceIDToCID: Tests HTTP client integration, error handling (400), and payload formatting.
  • TestValidateAndSyncCID: Verifies cache update dispatch on CID mismatch and fast-return behavior when CID matches.

5. Deployment Guide

Deploying via Docker Compose:

  1. Ensure the branch is checked out and updated: 
    cd /home/typesense/go-search-address
git pull origin feat/validate-cid-convert
  2. Rebuild and restart the container: 
    docker-compose up -d --build
  3. Inspect logs to verify startup: 
    docker logs -f --tail=100 go-search-address-places-api-1

Description:

Investigate and fix an issue where importing virtual tours published via third-party tools (such as Matterport) from Google results in incorrect CID assignments. Update the import pipeline to resolve the accurate CID by extracting it directly from the PlaceID using the existing extraction helper.
